meta.title: Pikadoku: Daily Pokémon Sudoku
meta.description: Pikadoku is Pokémon Sudoku, a free Pokémon grid game: fill a 3×3 grid with a Pokémon that fits each row and column. Easy, Normal and Expert dailies, a rarity score, unlimited grids and Tic Tac Toe duels.

info.description: Pikadoku is a free Pokémon Sudoku and Pokémon grid game: fill a 3×3 grid with a different Pokémon in each cell, matching both its row and its column.
info.intro: Pikadoku is Pokémon Sudoku: a 3×3 Pokémon grid game with a new puzzle every day, in Easy, Normal and Expert.

steps.read: Read the three row and three column categories: types, regions, evolution, moves, abilities, stats and more.
steps.tap: Tap a cell and search for a Pokémon that fits both its row and its column. It locks in if it is right.
steps.pp: You have 9 guesses (PP) in a daily, and a wrong guess still uses one. Each Pokémon can be used once.
steps.score: Your rarity score is the sum of the share of players who picked the same answers: lower is rarer, and better.
steps.end: When the game ends, see every valid answer for every cell and why your misses did not fit.

faq.scoreQ: How is the score worked out?
faq.scoreA: It is the sum of the percentage of players who picked each of your answers in that cell, worked out by the server from recorded answers. Lower means rarer picks and a better score.
faq.formsQ: How do forms and regions count?
faq.formsA: Regional forms, Megas, Gigantamax forms and a few notable forms (like Partner Pikachu) are their own picks, with their own types, stats and abilities. A species' region is where it debuted; a regional form counts for the region it debuted in (Alolan Raichu is Alola), and Mega and Gigantamax forms count for their species' region. A form and its species are the same Pokémon, so only one of them can be used in a grid.
faq.solvableA: Yes. Every daily is checked so each cell has enough valid answers and nine different Pokémon can fill the grid.
faq.levelsQ: What are Easy, Normal and Expert?
faq.levelsA: Easy uses broad categories with many answers, Normal is the main grid for the leaderboard, and Expert uses harder categories like moves, abilities and stat thresholds.

duel.about: A Pikadoku Tic Tac Toe duel: take turns claiming cells with a Pokémon that fits, and get three in a row.
duel.challenges: {host} challenges you to Pikadoku Tic Tac Toe
